coverage.reason: Interpreted for addressed actors, defined products, exemption and duration.
Original commencement explains the date; insignificant exposures and regulatory alignment are rationale, not individual eligibility conditions.
EU background; its reporting conditions and permanence are not expressly incorporated into the SFC exemption.
UK background; publication date and indefinite duration do not determine SFC eligibility.
Future amendment and gazettal are preserved without inventing a commencement prerequisite.
Invitation to direct queries to a case officer, not an application or approval condition.
Identifies the relevant margin regime; its detailed applicability remains unresolved because the Code is absent.
Citation to overseas background authority; its contents are not supplied.
Citation to UK background authority; its contents are not supplied.
Defines the referenced UK standards, not SFC product or actor eligibility.

dimensions.explanation: The circular addresses licensed corporations. Whether an assessed corporation and obligation fall within the underlying margin regime requires the missing Code. Neither the Code's title nor the selected slice establishes a definition of classified licensed corporations.

The collective term covers the three enumerated option categories, each subject to non-central clearing. It does not define actor classification or extend expressly to every equity-linked derivative, embedded option or mixed contract.

The exemption attaches to the specified products under the identified SFC margin regime. Insignificant exposures explain the decision; EU reporting conditions do not become SFC conditions through the alignment rationale.

The SFC announces that it will exempt the products. This supports an announced exemption predicate, not whole-entity compliance, a prohibition on collecting margin, or a requirement to obtain case-officer approval.

The announced start is 4 January 2026, with continuation until further notice. No execution-date cutoff, fixed expiry or gazettal prerequisite is stated. Subsequent notices and transitional treatment remain unresolved.

Part III of Schedule 10, including paragraph 7(e), is necessary to determine underlying applicability and implementation. Overseas references provide background. The three opaque missing-dependency identifiers cannot be mapped to authorities from this packet.

questions: What actor classifications and applicability conditions does Part III of Schedule 10 impose, including any definition of classified licensed corporations?
Do the Code or implementing instruments specify treatment of mixed contracts, embedded options, existing transactions or accrued obligations?
Has a subsequent SFC notice become effective for the assessed transaction and date, and what is its effect?
What amendment and gazettal occurred, and which named authorities correspond to the three missing-dependency identifiers?

assumptions: The selected control concerns one corporation, one option transaction, one otherwise applicable margin obligation and one assessment date.
Actor classification and underlying regime applicability are distinct from membership in the circular's defined product category.
The collective definition applies non-central clearing to all three enumerated option categories.
The express commencement date governs the announced position; future amendment and gazettal are not added as unstated conditions precedent.
Unknown classification, underlying applicability and subsequent-notice facts remain unknown.

citations.quote: issues this circular to inform licensed corporations
non-centrally cleared single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options (collectively, “non-centrally cleared equity options”)
considering that licensed corporations’ exposures to non-centrally cleared equity options are currently insignificant
subject to monitoring and periodic reporting2.
It implemented an indefinite exemption from the UK bilateral margining requirements for single-stock equity options and index options.
Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.
Should you have any queries regarding the contents of this circular, please contact your case officer.
As set out in Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Code of Conduct).

readings.distinction: The scope-and-definition challenge supports retaining the parent's substantive control. Being a licensed corporation does not itself establish that the margin regime otherwise applies; being an equity-linked instrument does not itself establish membership in the three defined option categories. The source does not support a rival extending eligibility to registered persons merely because they appear in the Code's title, restricting eligibility by an invented insignificant-exposure threshold, or requiring case-officer approval. Likewise, importing overseas qualifications or making gazettal a prerequisite lacks sufficient textual support. These failed hypotheses do not justify a second formalization. The strongest uncertainty is the missing Code's detailed actor and product scope. The reported incomparable fact bindings provide no substantive counterexample or basis for changing the preserved fact definitions.

facts.meaning: The assessed corporation is a licensed corporation addressed by the SFC circular.
facts.name: is_licensed_corporation

facts.meaning: The assessed margin obligation for this corporation and transaction would fall within Part III of Schedule 10 absent this announced exemption, taking other applicable scope conditions into account.
facts.name: otherwise_within_margin_requirements

facts.meaning: The assessed option transaction is not centrally cleared.
facts.name: is_non_centrally_cleared

facts.meaning: The assessed instrument is a single-stock option, equity basket option or equity index option within the circular's listed categories.
facts.name: is_listed_equity_option

facts.meaning: The date for which applicability of the announced exemption is assessed.
facts.name: assessment_date

facts.meaning: On the assessment date, no subsequent SFC notice has become effective that ends or displaces the announced exemption for this assessed transaction. Absence of such a notice from this packet does not establish this fact.
facts.name: announcement_remains_applicable

questions: Does the underlying Code narrow the addressed population or any enumerated product category?
What evidence establishes that the announcement remains applicable to the assessed transaction on the assessment date?
readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within the scope of a licensed corporation and an otherwise applicable Part III of Schedule 10 margin obligation, true means the assessed transaction satisfies the proposed announced-exemption conditions: it is non-centrally cleared, belongs to one of the three listed option categories, is assessed on or after 4 January 2026, and the announcement remains applicable. False means at least one condition fails; it does not establish that margin is owed under other rules. Outside that scope this control supplies no applicability decision. Unknown facts remain unknown.
readings.subject: Applicability of the announced SFC equity-option margin exemption
